sources.citation: Glottolog 5.x languoid record uain1239 (Glottolog's most extensive description = wordlist or less; refs Wallace 1853, Martius 1867, Ramirez 2001, Ramirez 2020:359-360, 429-539).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)

sources.citation: Wallace, Alfred R. 1853. A narrative of travels on the Amazon and Rio Negro, with an account of the native tribes.. London: Reeve. Appendix 'Vocabularies of Amazonian languages' pp.521ff (Uainambeu = Wainumá among ten vocabularies), with R. G. Latham's 'Remarks on the vocabularies' pp.525ff.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Only a transcription convention, p.521 (pdf p.555): 'the accent shows where the stress is to be laid' -- i.e. stress is marked per word in the Uainambeu list; no generalization about where it falls. Latham's remarks are on lexical/pronominal affinities only. (The folding vocabulary sheet itself is not in this Smithsonian scan; Martius 1867 re-lists Wallace's Uainambeu items marked 'W.'.)

sources.citation: Portuguese Wikipedia, 'Língua wainumá-mariaté' (tables copied from Ramirez 2020, Enciclopédia das línguas Arawak vol. II pp.157-159: retranscribed Wainumá/Mariaté forms and Wainumá-Mariaté : Baniwa-Koripako segmental correspondences).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: No stress statement; Ramirez's retranscribed forms carry acute accents on some words (atápʊi, apá-keri, kapéna, pítʃaka, ipʊ́ri..) reproduced from the 19th-c. sources; the correspondence table is segmental only.

sources.citation: Adelaar, Willem F. H. & Hélène B. Brijnen. 2014. Johann Natterer and the Amazonian languages. Revista Brasileira de Linguística Antropológica 6(2): 333-352. doi:10.26512/rbla.v6i2.16285
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on Wainumá stress. p.338: Natterer's 'Unainuman (possibly Vuainuman)' list from a tributary of the Içá 'is rather incomplete' and unidentified; pp.339-340 discuss Natterer's diacritics in general (acute on é sometimes marks a central vowel, not stress).

sources.citation: Ramirez, Henri. 2001. Línguas Arawak da Amazônia Setentrional: comparação e descrição. Manaus: EDUA. sec. 4.3.25 'Os Wainuma e os Mariaté', printed pp.371-382 (pdf 381-392).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.harvard_location: Tozzer Library (offsite storage), call number PM5476 .R36 2001
sources.note: Nothing. 'Sobre a língua destes dois povos, só encontrei listas de vocábulos em Martius (1863).' Gives history, 84.5% Wainumá-Mariaté shared vocabulary, lexicostatistic percentages (Yukuna 69%), a few affixes extracted from Martius, and re-lists the Martius wordlists; no phonology, no accent remark anywhere in the section.

sources.citation: Martius, Carl Friedrich Phil. von. 1867. Beiträge zur Ethnographie und Sprachenkunde Amerika's zumal Brasiliens. II: Wörtersammlung / Glossaria linguarum brasiliensium. Leipzig: Fleischer. 'Uainumá' pp.245-249 (Martius on the Yupurá; Spix items 'S.', Wallace items 'W.'), 'Mariaté' pp.266-268 (Spix, mouth of the Içá).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: No statement. Wordlists carry acute accents on individual words (e.g. amáhrai-ápe 'aër'); footnote p.245 only explains Wallace's orthography (vowels as in Portuguese, consonants as in English, til = nasal, raised letters faintly sounded); Mariaté footnote p.266 only says 'Auch Muriaté genannt.. dem der Uainumá näher'. The accent remark on p.29 concerns Tupi orthography.

sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing; lists collectors (Spix & Martius 1820, Natterer 1832, Wallace 1851) and classification (Kaufman 1994, Ramirez 2020).
